# ui::Clipboard

Header: `winui/ui/Clipboard.hpp`.

The system clipboard as a control or app sees it: text, a bitmap and storage items.

The library provides the implementation. There is one for the whole process, returned by [ui::clipboard()](namespace-ui.md#clipboard). [TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox)'s Ctrl+C/X/V and every other control go through it, and app code uses it the same way, also before [ui::run()](namespace-ui.md#run). A test swaps in a double with [`ui::testing::set_clipboard()`](../testing/namespace-ui-testing.md#set_clipboard). Non-copyable. The library owns it.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Clipboard& clipboard = ui::clipboard();
clipboard.set_text("Copied!");
if (clipboard.contains(ui::StandardDataFormat::Bitmap))
{
    const std::optional<ui::Bitmap> picture = clipboard.bitmap();
}
// Keep the subscription alive for as long as the notifications are wanted.
ui::ButtonControl paste_button{"Paste"};
ui::Subscription  paste_watch = clipboard.content_changed().observe([&](const std::uint64_t&) {
    paste_button.set_enabled(clipboard.contains(ui::StandardDataFormat::Text));
});
```

## set_text

```cpp
virtual void set_text(const std::string& text) = 0
```

Replace the clipboard's contents with [`text`](#text).

## text

```cpp
virtual std::optional<std::string> text() const = 0
```

The clipboard's current text, or nullopt if it holds no text (empty, or a non-text format like an image). Holding an empty string returns "", not nullopt.

## set_content

```cpp
virtual bool set_content(const ClipboardContent& content, const ClipboardContentOptions& options = {}) = 0
```

Replace the clipboard's contents with every part of [`content`](spec-vocabulary.md#content) that is set. False when the clipboard could not be opened (another app holds it) or [`content`](spec-vocabulary.md#content) has nothing in it; the old contents are then left alone.

Works from any thread. A large bitmap takes a while to encode, so an app copying one can call it from a background thread to keep its window responsive.

## bitmap

```cpp
virtual std::optional<Bitmap> bitmap() const = 0
```

The clipboard's picture, or nullopt when it holds none or it cannot be decoded.

## storage_items

```cpp
virtual std::vector<std::filesystem::path> storage_items() const = 0
```

The paths on the clipboard; empty when it holds none.

## requested_operation

```cpp
virtual DataPackageOperation requested_operation() const = 0
```

What the app that copied the storage items wants done with them, such as Move after a cut in a file manager. None when it said nothing.

## contains

```cpp
virtual bool contains(StandardDataFormat format) const = 0
```

Whether the clipboard holds data in `format`.

## available_formats

```cpp
virtual std::vector<std::string> available_formats() const = 0
```

The name of every format on the clipboard, in the order its owner put them there. These are the system's format names, such as "CF_UNICODETEXT", "PNG" or "CF_HDROP". Empty when the clipboard is empty.

## clear

```cpp
virtual void clear() = 0
```

Empty the clipboard.

## is_history_enabled

```cpp
virtual bool is_history_enabled() const = 0
```

Whether the user has turned on the clipboard history (Win+V).

## is_roaming_enabled

```cpp
virtual bool is_roaming_enabled() const = 0
```

Whether the user has turned on syncing the clipboard across devices.

## content_changed

```cpp
const Property<std::uint64_t>& content_changed()
```

A count of clipboard changes. It goes up every time any app, this one included, changes the clipboard. Observe it to get notified of changes, and drop the [Subscription](../core/subscription.md) to stop. The clipboard is only watched from the first call on.

## start_watching

```cpp
virtual void start_watching()
```

Starts watching for clipboard changes. Called once, on the first [content_changed()](#content_changed).

## raise_content_changed

```cpp
void raise_content_changed()
```

Advances [content_changed()](#content_changed) by one; an implementation calls it on every change it sees, its own writes included.
